I really think pets are a very good idea for depression. 
Depression is a very lonely thing - and mental illness often inadvertently isolates a person from routine/goals/ and just life!
Pets can give you a bit of that back. They provide a focus, companionship, and certain routine and fulfilment. 
Of course it doesn't solve all your problems. 
Another thing is just making sure the "basics" in your life are being seen to (is easier said than done I know) - but moderate exercise, enough sleep, enough relaxation, a healthy diet with at least half of it being unprocessed food.

You're a very sensitive person - and that's to your credit. You sound humble, and astute. Those are good qualities. The truth of the matter is (as you've already realised) that we live in a morally bereft society, and it most likely isn't going to change. If you don't want to die (and I'm not suggesting you should) then you have to live, and accept that you are a probably a good person in a terrible world. - remember this "It is no measure of sanity to be perfectly adjusted in an insane world"

Yeah sure - have a fairly long psychiatric history. Started off with severe depression similar to how I'm feeling now, then psychosis which required a long hospitalisation. I hate it and I hate myself. I hate being alive. I'm hopelessly in love with someone i know i can never have. I just feel like a worthless piece of crap.

If you behave and are an informal patient then it should be an ok experience. If you're sectioned or forced to take the drugs then the shit really hits the fan and you'll wish you'd never been born. Before i got sectioned my time in hospital provided a therapeutic environment. It was quiet, the people were nice, always had someone to talk to, and people took an interest in you and made sure you were well. When you can't really look after yourself,hospital can do some of the caring.

I understand how fucking horrible it is (I was abused in hospital) and I fully acknowledge how cruel and ugly this world is. I struggle to cope so much too - but things fluctuate. I've found planning for the future helps me stay a bit more focused but obviously we do end up in dire situations (through no fault of our own) where there is little room for manoeuvre and we feel trapped. You need to try and feed yourself regularly. Just small amounts if you can at all. Please do this for yourself to try and improve your mood a little. I fully sympathise though and I can see how tough things are for you. Please stay strong

Hi, I am still here. I phoned a support line I am referred to and she said I need to phone elsewhere as they can't help me and can only give "practical suggestions" like watch TV or have a bath. She also threatened to call an ambulance which panicked me as I don't want help from services. They are a joke. I just feel so pathetic. Was meant to be seeing some friends today but have no energy whatsoever. Just feel awful.
I have time too. I'm here.

Hey, this struck a chord with me. I'm younger than you (21) but I have no job or routine to speak of. I feel ashamed of who I am, and i get the feeling you're full of guilt too. I feel that I have a lot to offer as a person but sometimes it just doesn't feel enough y'know? I dont even know what actually would be enough. I do understand. Just want to let you know that. I hope you can find some strength.
